description: A printed basic wire holder converts a 6-position header_long with equal pin ends into a 3-contact connector. Empty plastic cells locate the header in the plate.
steps: Cut one 6-position section of header_long (6.25 mm exposed at both ends). Count from the key side (negative X in the model) and push out pins 1, 2, 6; keep the full plastic strip.
Pass 3 wires up through the rear opening before crimping. Crimp one socket per wire and insert the sockets into the backs of the housings until latched.
Mate the housing with the rear 6.25 mm pin ends, then lower the header and housing into their seats. The equal front ends face the front opening.
Check that the wires move freely through the rear opening and the contacts remain recessed inside the front edge.
note: The stock and prepared header rows describe the same item before and after modification. Use 15 mm overall header_long stock (6.25 mm exposed on each side of a 2.5 mm insulator); LCSC C343639 is a 40-position strip cut to the required lengths. Wire colours identify conductors, not a pinout. Housing and uncrimped socket geometry use nominal Harwin M20 references; wire bends are illustrative.
